- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f1e921ab8ebfe061baec70b6113dee12b6360b4f` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa949a84f2d0ac28cce7af4d1706d03c06d02431`
Local-runs: none

Read-only review of PR #20642 (stage 10 of #20233, the last) at the head above, against `main` at the merge base `a918fe7fd0`, rendered 2026-09-29T12:55Z. Inputs: the card's body and all 37 comments (in particular stage 9's landing `5889476387`, the stage-10 claim `5889494040` and the stage-10 report `5890543205`), stage 9's PR #20630 and its at-tier record `5889122134`, ruling C+D on #19123 (`5749154545`), the sources the new sentences read from (card #17360, objectui#7347 analysis `5615378321` and ruling record `5615810454`, objectui's `AGENTS.md` rule 0.1 at blob `534a8ee514`, card #4001 comments `5165088968` / `5171124152` / `5173360676`), the PR's body, its one comment, its 7-file list and the net diff, and the head's check-runs read once. Every count below is my own reading of `git show` objects through a scratch tokenizer (no checkout, no build, no test, no gate); every sentence judgment is against the cited record, not the dev's prose.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set: unchanged — RIGHT.** The diff touches no Zod schema, conversion, matcher, `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `acceptanceCriteria`, `from` / `to`, import or comment. My token-skeleton comparison of all 318 semantic entry files at base and head (every string literal collapsed, adjacent concatenations merged, comments dropped) reports 0 structural differences. A per-field extraction of the three entries' five fields at base and head finds exactly three fields changed, all `reason`; the other twelve are byte-equal. `registry.ts` parses to 367 entries at both refs with exactly three changed fields, the same three `reason`s, and each registry copy equals its entry copy byte-for-byte at head (lengths 3640 / 2204 / 1792).
2. **Public surface: author-shown guidance text only — RIGHT.** `@objectstack/spec` ships the registry, so the `why:` line `os migrate meta` prints changes for three entries and nothing else; no export is added or removed (Build Core and Type Check · source gates are green at this head; `check:api-surface` unchanged per the dev, judged by the still-running Type Check and Lint jobs).
3. **The three projections are exact — RIGHT.** The four `registry.ts` hunks sit inside the `reason` fields of `ui-notification-action-embed-config-retired` (two hunks), `ui-list-view-groupbyfield-padded-refused` and `ui-list-view-grouping-field-padded-refused`, verified by the nearest preceding `id:` and key. `spec-changes.json` (both its `aggregate` and `perMajor` copies) and `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` carry the notification entry's head text: `batch 14` and `That batch` read 2 / 1 at base and 0 / 0 at head in the two files. The two protocol-18 entries are absent from both projections at base and at head (0 hits on either id), as the released-majors-only design says; `AGENTS.md #0.1` reads 0 in both at both refs, so nothing there was ever stale.
4. **Census — reproduced.** Whole tree, 318 entries, four printed fields: base `a918fe7fd0` 0 tracker ids (# plus 4-5 digits) in every field, 0 in `surface`, 10 short numbers, all in `reason`: `#10` x4, `#12` x3, `#2` x1 and `#0.1` x2. Head: 0 / 0 / 8, the same eight Prime Directive references in the same eight entries; the two `#0.1` are gone. Tracker ids inside comment tokens read 143 at both refs (an occurrence count, so not the dev's 126-line figure, and equal on both sides). This repository's `AGENTS.md` carries `#0.1` 0 times at base and at head, so the reference was dangling here exactly as the stage-9 review escalated.
5. **The two `ui-list-view-*` sentences — RIGHT, true to the source, nothing lost, nothing added.** The number named rule 0.1 of objectui's contributor guide, «Fix the metadata, not the renderer (contract-first)», which card #17360's body cites as the governing text («fix the producer, do not teach the renderer to tolerate») and which the batch-110 item-5 analysis names as its governing text before the maintainer's 「其他同意」. The new parenthetical says: fix the metadata, not the renderer — the rule's title; off-spec metadata is refused where it is authored — the rule's «fix it at the producer (and have it rejected at authoring/publish)»; never coerced into working — the rule's «do not add a lenient fallback/alias in the renderer (… coercing a malformed shape …) to make non-compliant metadata work». Each clause maps to a clause of the source and none goes beyond it. The ruling record's own operative sentence (refuse at the producer with a non-padded pattern, not `.trim()` because that makes the padded and unpadded spellings silently equivalent) is the sentence these `reason`s already carried and still carry, untouched around the edit. Consistency with stage 9: the `address-` entry reads «(contract-first — fix the metadata, not the runtime)», this repository's Prime Directive 12 title; these two read «the contract-first rule … (fix the metadata, not the renderer: …)», objectui's rule title. Same form (the rule named as contract-first and stated in words, no number), each in the wording of the source its ruling actually cited; for entries whose subject is the renderer's readers and objectui's harvester trim, «renderer» is the truer word. The dev's offered two-line swap to the stage-9 parenthetical is not needed; it is the seat's taste if it wants one spelling.
6. **The batch ordinal — RIGHT under form D, and the edited sentence is still true.** «its ui/ batch 14» is row 14 of the plan table in card #4001's comment `5165088968` (action + notification + sharing + report + dataset + dashboard), claimed in `5171124152` and accepted in `5173360676`. That is a pointer into a tracker object, which is the dependency form D removes (`5749154545`: «the lesson is written into the text»), and the claim's keep-arm («if it names nothing an author must look up») does not apply because a plan row is exactly something to look up. What the batch measured and decided is already in the sentence and I read it back against the source: `5171124152` dispatches the batch with «逐文件先测门（承载键 + BFS 可达 + parse 站点）» — the door measured per file, three ways, before any closing; `5173360676` (2026-08-04) accepts 9 tightened and 2 reclassified as no-door (`EmbedConfig` «全仓零提及改判») and routes #5015 (`NotificationAction` / `EmbedConfig` 无门退役) to REMOVE. So «did NOT close them with `.strict()` … left the disposition to ADR-0049's enforce-or-remove, which came back REMOVE on 2026-08-04» holds. Re-pointing «That batch» to «The sweep» keeps it true: the batch is part of the sweep, and the relative clause «which measured each ui/ file for an authoring door before closing any shape» was already attached to the sweep at base, so its reach is unchanged by the edit. Precedent: stage 6's report `5881313353` dropped the same campaign's «批 20» the same way. The two remaining `batch` tokens in printed prose at head are file names (`-ui-batch13` etc. as changeset file names in `authoring-schemas-strict-unknown-keys`, and `spec-symbol-batch7.test.ts` in `ui-widget-i18n-family-retired`), not plan ordinals, and outside this claim.
7. **Scope — RIGHT.** The 7 files are the three entries the stage-9 landing named, their three projections, and one changeset: the claim's surface and nothing wider. No `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `skills/**` or `NORTH-STAR` path; Governed Surface Queue Guard is green. Head repo equals base repo; draft; assignee `os-tesla` equals the card's; 42 / 11 lines.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **`patch`**, `Clause-②: no` — RIGHT. Author-shown guidance text in a published package changes, so `skip-changeset` would be wrong; no accept set, export or authorable key moves, so `minor` is not owed and no widening / narrowing arm applies. The changeset body carries the standalone `Clause-②: no` line and the PR body carries it as its own line; the changeset names the three entries, says text only, and carries no tracker number and no model identifier. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1 (batch ordinal: DROP rather than keep or restate):** answered in ①.6 — right; the restatement the claim's first arm asked for was already in the sentence.
- **Dev deviation 2 (rule stated from objectui's rule 0.1 rather than this repository's Prime Directive 12):** answered in ①.5 — right; no swap required.
- **Dev deviation 3 (stage-9 instruments reused):** their readings are reproduced here by an independent tokenizer (0 / 0 / 10 to 0 / 0 / 8; 3 fields; 0 skeleton changes).
- **Dev deviations 4-8 (lock holds, CLI unit and typecheck not run locally, attribution form, no label writes, main not merged, teardown):** bookkeeping. CLI unit and typecheck are Test Core's and Type Check's readings, still running at read time; `registry.ts` moved on `main` only under paths this diff does not touch per the dev's driver-free merge-tree, and GitHub reports the PR mergeable. If the queue reports a conflict there, regenerate, never hand-merge.
- **Out-of-scope finding: five code comments citing `AGENTS.md #0.1`** (`ui/view.zod.ts` x2, `ui/component.zod.ts` x1, `ui/view.test.ts` x2, verified by `git grep` on the head tree): not printed by `os migrate meta`, so outside this card's positions; a comment's reader is a contributor with the sibling checkout, and the reference is a rule number, not a tracker number, so it is not #20234's population either — at most a cosmetic «objectui's» that lane may add when it touches those lines. Nothing owed here. For completeness the same string also stands in `packages/console/CHANGELOG.md` (1) and `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md` (1), which the dev's list does not name; both are records, equally outside.
- **Out-of-scope finding: four released `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` entries** carry the same string (count verified 4): release-owned, never edited in a code PR, not printed by the migrator; not a factual error, so no docs-only PR is owed. Correctly left.
- **Out-of-scope finding: the pin's detector reads `#` plus 4-5 digits only:** as stage 9's record already held, a batch ordinal without `#` is held by review, which is what this review did. Not this card's.
- **Out-of-scope finding: changeset file names in `authoring-schemas-strict-unknown-keys`'s `reason`:** file names, not numbers, outside the card's rule and the claim; if the seat treats «provenance an author cannot open» as its own class, that is a bare card, not a hold on this one.
- **The eight Prime Directive references that stay:** the claim fences them and the stage-9 record judged them contributor-guide rule references, not tracker ids; they resolve in this repository's `AGENTS.md`, which is the distinction from the dangling `#0.1`. Outside the card's population. Noted only: an author's own project holds neither guide, so if the seat ever wants those eight in words too, it is a separate card.
- **Card population and closing keyword:** the card's defect is tracker numbers in the printed fields of the semantic entries; that population is 0 at base and at head, and the three items stage 9's landing record named as «what is left on this card» are the three this diff delivers. `Fixes #20233` is the shape the claim set for the last stage; the card's newest `Claim:` names this branch and the claim-parity check is green. Nothing else is owed on the card. Closing it is the seat's landing act with a closing record.
- **Check-runs, read once:** 32 on the head: 14 success, 3 skipped by design at this path set (Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke), 0 failing, **15 not concluded at read time:** Test Core 1/6 through 6/6 (the CLI guidance pin and the spec suites), Dogfood Regression Gate 1/3 through 3/3, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Type Check · workspace, · consumer gates, · debt ledger, and Lint & Repo Gates (`check:doc-authoring`, `check:migration-registry`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:generated`). Green: Build Core (which also answers the dev's one NOT MEASURED family, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`), Type Check · source gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, the card-claims-this-branch and Part-of checks, the same-issue and single-writer-path checks, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Auto Label and filter. This verdict judges the diff; landing still waits for every required context to conclude green.
